newsitem.title: USA: Egypt considers 55,000-110,000 T U.S. wheat - trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt considers 55,000-110,000 T U.S. wheat - trade.

text.p: Egypt was considering the purchase of 55,000 to 110,000 tonnes U.S. hard red winter wheat for June 1-10 delivery, several U.S. exporters said.
"It would be our new crop" and the first major new crop business for the United States, a U.S. exporter said.
Egypt was reported to be tendering on Wednesday night for a total of 165,000 tonnes if U.S. or Australian wheat.

The wheat was to be divided between three positions of 55,000 tonnes each. One lot was slated for April 1-10 delivery, the second for May 1-10 and the third for June 1-10. The first two positions were expected to go to Australia, exporters said.
"The tender was still under consideration," the exporter said. "They (Egypt) would like to buy 55,000 to 110,000 tonnes U.S. wheat for that time position."
He noted for the June time slot, the U.S. wheat was fairly competitive. "But nothing has been confirmed." he said.
But one U.S. exporter said Egypt already bought on Wednesday night 55,000 tonnes U.S. wheat for the June slot at about $166 a tonne cost and freight. "They bought it last night," he said.
